stopped_items: H1 (the whole of it) — the command-string bound on all ten census jobs. Measured unbuildable, not deferred: it breaks every procedure it would be applied to. Nothing was altered. Successor filed as FIX-1185.
Item 3 (migration 2, cron.alter_job by name on ~8 jobs) — not written. It is H1.
H2 (record-and-STOP handlers in the three C1 procedures) — already built. No procedure redefined; prod md5s unchanged and identical to the Phase 0 baseline.
H4 (the general command-string sweep) — NOT filed as written, because the mechanism it would sweep does not work. Redirected into FIX-1185, which asks which bound replaces it.
H5's clone proof of the three procedures under a command-string bound — cannot be run. The form does not bound them, it stops them at their first COMMIT.
Item 6 (the Pattern B record commit closing FIX-1128) — condition does not hold, and cannot: there is no new command string for a daily to run under. FIX-1128 stays open pending FIX-1185.

The check:proconfig fixture for the cron.alter_job command-string shape — deliberately not added. The scanner already agrees (an existing fixture covers a SET inside a quoted string), and a fixture blessing that shape would lock in the pattern this run refutes. The scanner's failure message, which recommended it, was corrected instead.

rule-taggers-daily's 7200 s budget is the one place where a computed bound sits below an observed maximum (14,028.2 s, 2026-08-05). Built rather than stopped, with the evidence in the migration header, and revertible by one DELETE. Reasoning in section 9.
